predecessors.name: Buyid dynasty
predecessors.text: the fortresses around Qarmisin (Kermanshah) that Hasanwayh gathered after the deaths of two uncles in 960 and 961

successors.name: Annazids
successors.text: Shahrizor (recaptured by Abu al-Fath ibn Annaz in 1013) and the Jibal lands: "the Annazid rule in the Jibal replaced that of the Hasanwayhids"

successors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
successors.text: Kermanshah, listed as a later successor in the infobox

rulers.name: Badr ibn Hasanwayh (Abu al-Najm, Nasir al-Dawla)

ledger.x: 959: Hasanwayh ibn Husayn founds the Hasanwayhid emirate (infobox 959-1015); 'the deaths of two uncles in 960 and 961 let him gather fortresses around Qarmisin (Kermanshah)'.
1015: the Annazids replace the Hasanwayhids in the Jibal.
1015: the Hasanwayhid emirate ends (infobox disestablished 1015); the family kept the fortress of Sarmaj, where the last heir died in 1047.

wars.name: Hasanwayhid-Annazid war over Shahrizor
wars.outcome: Badr expelled Abu al-Fath ibn Annaz; hostilities resumed in 1006-1007 and in 1013 Abu al-Fath recaptured Shahrizor; the Annazids replaced the Hasanwayhids in the Jibal after Badr's death in 1014.

certainty.note: A Kurdish fortress emirate named by towns (Dinavar, Nahavand, Borujerd, Shahrizor); the page gives no frontiers and no dates for the holdings.
